raw: {"analysis":"Response WNG provides a more coherent and properly serialized delivery plan that respects the stated constraints. It correctly identifies that the kill switch decision logic must be independent of the model service, explicitly protects the billing aggregator by enforcing read-only access to the shared fallback file, mandates local testing before pushing to avoid CI costs, and routes security review and deployment approval through David Chen. Response JRW has some structural issues, including a confusing gate ordering where independent code review happens after CI (which contradicts the local-testing-first constraint) and an unclear canary deployment strategy that doesn't align with the locked production environment requiring David Chen's manual approval. WNG's plan is more actionable and realistic for the Friday deadline.","verdict":"WNG"}
